title: The verifier's key-ceremony checks: definitions, boards and pinned panels, with the rows 2.5, 3.1 and 3.2
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-ceremony-vectors.py, from ceremony-vectors.py, definition-vectors.py and board-vectors.py (independent Python implementations)

cases.description: Every seat qualifies; the board carries an abandoned run's transcript first, which the verifier passes over by hash.
Seat 4 sends nothing; three qualified seats meet k = 3.
Seats 3 and 4 answer wrongly: two qualified seats are below k = 3.
The definition names a transcript made for another definition's stub (four options): every signature fails under this definition's context (T-37).
The transcript the definition names has a trailing byte.
The definition binds a boarded payload of another record type: it fails decoding as a transcript, not missing.
The board carries only the abandoned run's transcript.
The transcript is boarded only in an entry of another election.
The bundle pins a 2-of-4 panel; the definition names the 3-of-4 one.
The profile pins transcript version 2, which this verifier can't read.
A 4-of-7 panel where seat 7 sends nothing: six qualified seats meet n − 1 (ADR 0006, rule 7).
A 4-of-7 panel where seats 6 and 7 send nothing: five qualified seats meet k = 4 but not n − 1 = 6.
A 4-of-7 panel where only seats 1 to 4 take part: exactly k, two short of n − 1.
